status: Prospective multi-instance engineering gate; no accuracy claim
author: https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam2
reuse: Keep native add_new_mask, persistent ID mapping, per-object banks, propagate_in_video, decoder and memory writer unchanged. The adapter shares weights but computes memberships separately for each object.
fixture: Real PolypGen frames with controlled two-instance prompts: divide each existing polyp mask at the prompted mask's median foreground x-coordinate. This is an engineering fixture, not genuine annotated multi-object data or a Dice benchmark.
cache_amendment: Before accuracy experiments: initial native comparisons exposed equal positional values but different strides on first versus cached PositionEmbeddingSine calls. Clear only the author's deterministic position-encoding cache before each new state, so all comparisons start cold. Retain exact values AND layout checks; no hash fields are ignored. Failed diagnostics are retained in gate v1/v2 folders.
checks: Zero-adapter masks, object scores, pointers, spatial memory and positional encodings equal native for both instances.
Both instances retain nonconsecutive IDs, distinct banks, and four-layer reads.
Per-object native and nonzero-adapter trajectories are unchanged by reversing registration order or tracking the other object separately.
Adding the second object after propagation begins preserves native behavior and does not retroactively add it to earlier output records.
Joint equal-instance training loss reproduces native at initialization and trains shared adapter weights through both independent banks.
Both regional and per-instance global control pass; frozen backbone hash remains unchanged.
interpretation: Object-relative background includes pixels outside the target instance, potentially another target. Regions identify predicted positions, not semantically pure features. Preserve native overlap handling; do not union instances. Real multi-object data and benchmark evaluator checks remain required.
